initialization_boundary.reason: The initialization session inspected current public sources only to verify benchmark scope. Those observations must not anchor the sealed blind atlas.

passes.focus: cycle upswing, tight supply, pricing power and supplier investment response
questions: Recall price, inventory, bit supply/demand, node transitions, capex, supplier actions and contemporaneous narratives by half-year or quarter.
Which actors, constraints or forecasts mattered then but are less salient today?

passes.focus: downcycle, pandemic demand shifts, inventory and renewed tightness
questions: Separate PC, server and mobile demand narratives from actual comparable observations.
Recall supplier cuts, capex decisions, node transitions and forecasts that were later revised.

passes.focus: inventory correction, price decline, production cuts and capex discipline
questions: Recall when different actors recognized the inventory problem and how expected normalization timing changed.
Look for early contrary signals, write-downs, utilization changes and failed demand narratives.

passes.focus: AI/HBM mix shift, conventional DRAM interaction, capacity allocation and advanced packaging constraints
questions: Recall HBM qualification/ramp expectations separately from later outcomes.
Recall how suppliers described conventional DRAM, HBM trade ratios, bit supply, capex and cleanroom constraints at each stage.
Recall product-generation transitions, applications, qualification timing, supply constraints and pricing/mix implications.
Do not assume product generations or supplier node labels are directly comparable.
Exhaust Samsung, SK hynix, Micron, CXMT, Nanya and forgotten/edge suppliers by period.
For each actor recall fabs, cuts, capex, node moves, product ramps, customer qualification, failures, old names and major strategic reversals.
Include downstream actors only where they create a specific DRAM demand or qualification lead.
Recall historical definitions and periods where the metric became non-comparable or especially important.
Identify likely primary or methodology-bearing source families for later verification without searching now.
Recall mechanisms linking price, inventory, utilization, capex, node migration, bit-per-wafer growth, qualification and effective supply.
Recall how HBM die usage, stacking, base die and packaging constraints may alter conventional DRAM supply or economics.
For every mechanism generate historical examples as leads, not conclusions.
Recall consensus, minority views, shortage/oversupply narratives, inventory normalization forecasts and capex-discipline claims by period.
Recall HBM TAM, AI demand, Chinese supply and conventional DRAM narratives as they were stated at the time, not with hindsight.
Recall historical node labels, product names, fab names, old company/project names, pricing terms, report-title phrases and terminology useful for lost-web search.
Prefer vocabulary that a current searcher would not naturally guess.
Recall delayed fabs, failed or slow node ramps, qualification misses, utilization cuts, write-downs, cancelled investments and product narratives that did not materialize.
Include suppliers or technologies that were important at the time but later became marginal.
Work backward to potential earlier demand, inventory, capex, node, supply and customer-ordering conditions.
Use the later downturn only to activate leads; never present the later outcome as information already known earlier.

passes.anchor: 2024-2026 HBM-driven DRAM product-mix and capacity-allocation shift
questions: Recall earlier product, packaging, customer, accelerator and supplier decisions that may have set up the later HBM shift.
Separate what was genuinely anticipated from what only became obvious after AI demand accelerated.

Recall semiconductor equipment, advanced packaging, foundry/base-die, cloud capex, GPU/platform, handset/PC, geopolitics, export controls and financing variables that directly changed DRAM conditions.
Do not expand adjacent sectors beyond claim-scoped DRAM effects.
For each famous cycle explanation generate at least two contemporaneously plausible alternatives.
State what historical evidence would distinguish the explanations.
Inspect the generated time × actor/product × metric matrix for suspicious blanks.
Ask what a long-tenured DRAM operator would say is missing if the atlas looks too much like a public market report.
Cluster duplicate leads and classify remaining gaps.
Judge whether three consecutive orthogonal passes have produced few new high-importance non-duplicate leads.

recursive_questions_for_high_importance_: Who else? Which other actors are connected?
What preceded it? Which earlier indicators or decisions existed?
What followed it? Which later actions or observations may be connected?
What was it called then? Which historical vocabulary should later search use?

objectives: resolve vague memory leads into exact company, fab, product, report and historical terminology
locate claim-scoped primary sources before secondary summaries
separate independent sources from repeated syndication
forbidden: promote search snippets into Fact or Judgment
delete a lead because search returns not found
treat repeated secondary coverage as independent proof
